post.description:
This request allows you to create either a one-time donation or a recurring plan. To create a recurring plan, you must include a `recurring_plan` object with the `frequency` parameter. If the object is not provided, a one-time donation will be created. All fields and values must meet the requirements of your campaign. Otherwise, an error will be returned. We do not format or verify addresses and emails that were sent through the API.

A Stripe payment method ID is required. For more details on how to create a payment method, refer to the Stripe Payment Methods documentation.

### Prerequisites Make sure you have: - A Stripe account that is connected to your Fundraise Up account and [activated](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/step-1/#creating-a-new-stripe-account). - An active campaign with a money-based payment method. - An API key with permission to create new donations. - Access to the Stripe API for the same Stripe account used as the Fundraise Up payment method, with the ability to [create Payment Methods](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods). Nonprofit organizations must meet PCI compliance requirements to ensure the secure processing of payment card data. Fundraise Up complies with these standards, but if an organization or its vendor uses direct API integration with Stripe to send raw card data (such as card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV codes), that organization or vendor is responsible for meeting broader PCI DSS requirements, such as SAQ D for merchants or higher. When using [Stripe Elements](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/elements), organizations remain responsible for PCI compliance, but the scope is reduced, typically to SAQ A, due to Stripe handling sensitive card data processing. If a third-party vendor manages card details (for example, in face-to-face or direct mail solutions), they must maintain their own PCI compliance (SAQ D or applicable), and the organization should document them as their third-party service provider.

get.description:
This request helps you track updates and changes in your account in the same way as in the [Audit Log](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/audit-log/). While the `Donations` endpoint shows the current state of a donation when queried, it doesn't reflect changes that happen after the initial creation (for example, finalized fees or status updates). The `Events` endpoint logs all updates as they occur, giving you the most current view of activity when you query it.

### Use cases
- **Retrieving finalized fees**. The `platform_fee` field in a donation will initially show 0 until Stripe finalizes the fee data. To get the updated fee values, use the `Events` endpoint to track the `donation.success` event, which confirms that the finalized fees have been updated.
- **Monitoring donation status changes**. Donations can move through multiple statuses — `pending`, `success`, `failed`, and more. Use the `Events` endpoint to track status changes. For example, a donation might be `pending` while awaiting payment processor confirmation and later transition to `success` or `failed`.
- **Tracking refunds and disputes**. If a donation is refunded or disputed, you'll receive corresponding events like `donation.refunded`, `donation.success_dispute_created`, or `donation.success_dispute_won`. This helps keep your records accurate without manually checking each donation.
- **Handling recurring plan updates**. Recurring donations generate events like `recurring_plan.activated`, `recurring_plan.failed`, or `recurring_plan.canceled`. Monitoring these events allows you to track subscription activities and take appropriate actions if a recurring payment fails or is canceled.
- **Updating supporter information**. When a supporter updates their information or requests personal data deletion, events like `supporter.updated` or `supporter.personal_data_deleted` are triggered. This is especially important for maintaining compliance with data protection regulations.
- **Monitoring tribute activity**. Use events like `tribute.created` or `tribute.updated` to keep track of tribute donations and ensure that tribute cards are sent as expected (`tribute.shared`).

Use this request to retrieve a paginated list of supporter records from your Fundraise Up account. Each record includes the latest contact details and other supporter-level fields, matching the data shown in the Supporters view in the Dashboard.

## About supporter contact data

The `address`, `phone`, and `employer` fields in supporter records reflect the most recent information provided by the supporter.

These fields are updated automatically when:

* The supporter makes a new donation using the same email address.
* A donation or recurring plan is edited in the Dashboard.
* The supporter updates their details in the Donor Portal.

Installments do not update supporter-level contact data.

You can't edit supporter contact fields through the API. To change them, update the associated donation or recurring plan — in the Dashboard at any time, or through the API within 24 hours of creation. The supporter record will reflect the updated values automatically.

This behavior applies only to changes made after June 2, 2025. Data collected earlier is not updated retroactively.

### Tracking updates using the Events endpoint

To monitor changes to supporter contact data, use the [Events endpoint](https://api.fundraiseup.com/v1/docs/#/operations/GetEvents). The following events may indicate a change to supporter contact fields:

* `supporter.updated` — supporter-level data has changed.
* `donation.updated` — contact fields on a donation were modified.
* `recurring_plan.details_updated` — a recurring plan was edited.

When you receive one of these events, use the corresponding endpoints to retrieve updated data:

* `GET /supporters/{id}` — get supporter-level contact information.
* `GET /donations/{id}` — get contact details specific to a donation.
* `GET /recurring_plans/{id}` — get contact details specific to a recurring plan.

info.title: Fundraise Up API
info.description:
1. [Overview](#/#overview) 2. [Limitations](#/#limitations) 3. [Key features](#/#key-features) 4. [Use cases](#/#use-cases) 5. [How to get API key](#/#how-to-get-api-key) 6. [Managing API keys](#/#managing-api-keys) 7. [Authentication](#/#authentication) 8. [Parent accounts and subaccounts](#/#parent-accounts-and-subaccounts) 9. [Rate limits](#/#rate-limits) 10. [Errors](#/#errors) 11. [Pagination](#/#pagination) 12. [Request IDs](#/#request-ids) 13. [Changes in API](#/#changes-in-api) ## Overview The Fundraise Up API gives you more control over your fundraising data. Use it to process offline donations through your Fundraise Up account and keep your CRM or other systems up to date with your fundraising activity. With the API, you can interact with these resources: - Donations — Create and update donations and their associated recurring plans (within 24 hours of creation, API-created only). - Recurring plans — Read recurring donation schedules. - Supporters — Access supporter details. - Events — Retrieve events from your Audit Log. - Donor Portal access links — Authenticate supporters in the Donor Portal. - Donor Portal recurring plan access links — Provide direct access to recurring plan settings. - Campaigns — List and retrieve campaign details, assign and unassign designations. - Designations — Create, update, delete, and list designations, including batch operations. - Designation groups — List and retrieve designation groups, assign and unassign designations. - Designation configurations — Access relationships between designations and campaigns. - Upgrade links — Generate upgrade links for one-time donations to convert them into recurring plans. ## Limitations - Most endpoints operate on a single object per request. Designation endpoints support batch operations for up to 100 items. - Updates to Donations and Recurring plans are restricted to the first 24 hours and apply only to API-created donations. - You can retrieve and export data only for Donations, Recurring plans, Supporters, Events, Campaigns, Designations, Designation groups, and Designation configurations. - The API supports the following payment methods: credit cards, debit cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, ACH US Direct Debit, BACS Direct Debit, and PAD (Canadian Pre-Authorized Debit). - For ACH US Direct Debit, BACS Direct Debit, and PAD (Canadian Pre-Authorized Debit) donations, Fundraise Up sends the mandate confirmation email to the supporter only when `supporter.email` is provided. Without an email, notifying the supporter about the direct debit mandate is the organization's responsibility. ## Key features - Architecture — Built on REST principles. - URLs — Provides predictable, resource-oriented URLs. - Requests — Accepts JSON-encoded request bodies with `Content-Type: application/json` header. - Responses — Returns JSON-encoded responses. - Standards — Uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs. ## Use cases There are a variety of use cases where you can integrate our API into your fundraising flow. In particular, you can use our API for: - Ticketing and events. - Face-to-face fundraising. - Direct mail campaigns. - Telefundraising. - Fundraising galas and dinners. - Analytics integrations. The API is not intended for migrating subscriptions from legacy systems. For migration purposes, please refer to our [Migration service](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/migration/). ## How to get API key To use the Fundraise Up API, you first need to generate an API key. Only users with the [Organization Administrator](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/team-settings/#organization-administrator) role can create and manage API keys. Follow these steps to create your API key: 1. Go to **[Dashboard](https://dashboard.fundraiseup.com/)** > **Settings** > **API keys**. 2. Click **Create API key**. 3. Enter a descriptive name for your API key. This name helps you identify different keys when you have multiple integrations. 4. Set permissions for your key. You can assign different permissions for Live and Test data independently: **Live data permissions:** - **Donations** — Read: access donation information; Write: create and update donations - **Recurring plans** — Read: access recurring donation schedules - **Supporters** — Read: access supporter information - **Events** — Read: retrieve events from your Audit Log - **Fundraisers** — Read: access supporter-created Fundraisers; Write: create and update Fundraisers - **Donor Portal access links** — Write: generate secure login links for your supporters - **Campaigns** — Read: list and retrieve campaigns; Write: assign and unassign designations - **Designations** — Read: list and retrieve designations; Write: create, update, and delete designations - **Designation groups** — Read: list and retrieve designation groups; Write: assign and unassign designations - **Designation configurations** — Read: access relationships between designations and campaigns - **Upgrade links** — Write: generate upgrade links for one-time donations **Test data permissions:** - **Donations** — Read: access test donation information; Write: create and update test donations - **Recurring plans** — Read: access test recurring donation schedules - **Supporters** — Read: access test supporter information - **Events** — Read: retrieve test events from your Audit Log You must select at least one permission in either Live or Test data. You can modify permissions later using the three-dot menu next to the key. 5. Click **Create API key**. 6. Copy and securely store your API key. You will only see it once and cannot retrieve it later. Your key is activated immediately and does not expire. ![Name.png](https://ucarecdn.com/ada1a533-786f-48af-9816-0b37aeb16417/newapikey.png) ## Managing API keys You can view all your API keys on the [API keys page](http://dashboard.fundraiseup.com/settings/api-keys). For each key, click the three-dot menu to manage its settings. You can edit the key name, modify its permissions, or delete it if you no longer need it. **Note for API keys created before [30th January 2026]**: These keys cannot be edited through Dashboard. To update permissions, create a new API key. Keys created before this release will be deactivated 6 months after the release date. If you're using a third-party provider to manage your donations, they must have permission to create [Payment Method](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods) entities in the same Stripe account as Fundraise Up.

If you suspect that your API key has been compromised, delete it immediately and generate a new key.

## Authentication Authenticate to the API using HTTP Bearer authentication. Include your API key in the `Authorization` header like this: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer test_…"`. Ensure that all API requests are made over HTTPS. Requests made over HTTP will not be accepted. Requests without proper authentication will also be rejected. ## Parent accounts and subaccounts Each API key allows you to create donations only for the account to which it belongs. Parent accounts cannot create donations and generate [Donor Portal access links](https://fundraiseup.com/docs/seamless-donor-portal/) for subaccounts using their parent API key. To create donations for a subaccount, you need to generate an API key within that specific subaccount and use it. However, the parent account can still view and manage all API keys, including those for subaccounts. Additionally, a parent account's API key can export data for both the parent account and its subaccounts. This makes it easy to keep track of both API key activity and export data across the parent account and its subaccounts. ![Parent accounts and subaccounts.png](https://ucarecdn.com/07b2584a-7a8d-43f9-9be6-832b02d2f04a/api-2.png) ## Rate limits To maintain stability and ensure reliable performance, the Fundraise Up API uses a concurrency-based request limit. ### Concurrency limit Each account can send up to 3 API requests in parallel. This applies to all endpoints and all API keys associated with the same account, whether test or live. When more than 3 requests are sent in parallel, only 3 will be processed. Any additional requests will be rejected with a `429 Too Many Requests` error and the code `concurrent_requests_limit_exceeded`. To avoid hitting the limit: - Keep your integration single-threaded and run requests sequentially — one after another. - If you use parallel requests, implement a queue to control concurrency. ### Subaccounts The limit applies to each account individually. Parent and subaccounts are counted separately. If your setup requires more parallel processing, you can distribute requests across multiple subaccounts. ## Errors Fundraise Up uses standard HTTP response codes to indicate the outcome of an API request: - `2xx` codes indicate successful requests. - `4xx` codes indicate client-side errors, such as missing parameters or failed charges. - `5xx` codes, which are rare, indicate server-side issues with Fundraise Up. Certain 4xx errors, such as a [declined card](https://docs.stripe.com/declines), will include an error code with a brief explanation. ## HTTP status codes | Code | Status | Explanation | | ------------------ | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 200 | OK | Everything worked as expected. | | 400 | Bad Request | The request was invalid, typically due to a missing required parameter. | | 401 | Unauthorized | No valid API key provided. | | 403 | Forbidden | The API key doesn't have permissions to perform the request. | | 404 | Not Found | The requested resource doesn't exist. | | 409 | Conflict | The request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the resource. This usually indicates a concurrency issue. | | 429 | Too Many Requests | Your organization has exceeded the allowed number of concurrent requests. Reduce the number of simultaneous requests to avoid this error. | | 500, 502, 503, 504 | Server Errors | Something went wrong on the Fundraise Up side. (These are rare.) | ### Attributes - `code`**: nullable string.** Short error code for some errors that can be handled programmatically. - `message`**: nullable string.** Human-readable error description. - `parameter`**: nullable string.** Parameter associated with the error. - `stripe_error`**: nullable dictionary.** Stripe-specific error details (see [Stripe API documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/api/errors).) ### Error codes | Error code | Explanation | | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `tokens_rate_limit_exceeded` | Too many API tokens used within a time period. | | `requests_rate_limit_exceeded` | Organization has reached the limit for API requests per period. | | `concurrent_requests_limit_exceeded` | Account has too many parallel requests. | | `stripe_rate_limit_exceeded` | Too many requests made to Stripe. | | `stripe_error` | Error related to Stripe payment processing. | | `not_found` | Requested resource could not be found. | | `update_expired` | Update attempted after the allowed time period. | | `update_conflict` | The request conflicts with another request. | | `parameter_unexpected` | Unexpected parameter provided in the request. | | `parameter_required` | Required parameter is missing from the request. | | `parameter_invalid` | Parameter provided is not valid. | | `image_source_unavailable` | Image could not be fetched from the provided `upload_url`. | | `payment_account_required` | Payment account setup is necessary. | Error codes may change over time. We'll update this article to reflect any changes. ## Pagination All API endpoints that list records display them in reverse chronological order and use cursor-based navigation for browsing through the list. To maintain consistent sorting and navigation, especially when entities have the same creation date, records are also sorted by identifier in reverse alphabetical order. This means that records are first sorted by creation date (newest to oldest), and then by identifier (Z to A). | **Parameter** | **Type** | **Description** | | ---------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `limit` | **optional**, 10 by default | This parameter specifies the number of records to display per page, ranging from 1 to 100. | | `starting_after` | **optional object ID** | A cursor for pagination. The `starting_after` parameter uses an existing object ID to define your position in the list. For example, if you fetch a list of items and receive 100 results, you can use the ID of the last object in that list as the `starting_after` parameter in your subsequent request to retrieve the next page of results. | | `ending_before` | **optional object ID** | A cursor for pagination. The `ending_before` parameter uses an existing object ID to define your position in the list. For example, if you fetch a list of items and receive 100 results, you can use the ID of the first object in that list as the `ending_before` parameter in your subsequent request to retrieve the previous page of results. | The parameters `starting_after` and `ending_before` are mutually exclusive. A page is returned in full or not at all. Every record on a page is assembled together with the records it references, such as the supporter, campaign and designation of a donation. If one of those records cannot be loaded, the request fails and no records from that page are returned. Records are never silently skipped, so a successful response always contains every record on the page that matches your query. | **List response format** | **Type** | **Description** | | ------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `data` | **array** | An array containing the entity records, paginated by any request parameters. | | `has_more` | **boolean** | Indicates whether there are more records available. For `starting_after`, it shows that there is a page with older records. For `ending_before`, it indicates that there is a page with newer records. | ## Request IDs Each API request includes response header `Request-Id` with unique value. To help us resolve issues faster, please include the `Request-Id` when contacting us about a specific request. ## Changes in API We prioritize stability and compatibility in our API. We aim to make all changes backwards-compatible within the current version to avoid disrupting your existing workflows. If a change requires incompatibility, we will release a new API version. Detailed information about any changes will be posted on this page and added to the documentation. ### September 2026 #### Updated `POST /v1/donations` `POST /v1/donations` now supports PAD (Canadian Pre-Authorized Debit). Pass a Stripe `acss_debit` payment method in `payment_method.stripe.id` together with `payment_method.stripe.setup_intent_id`. PAD is available only for organizations in Canada and the United States and for donations in CAD, supports both one-time and recurring donations, and does not support the daily and weekly frequencies. The mandate's payment schedule must match the donation: a `sporadic` mandate is accepted only for one-time donations, an `interval` mandate only for recurring plans, and a `combined` mandate for both. #### Added recurring_plan.reactivated_as_new_plan event type to GET /api/v1/events The `types` field now includes a new allowed value: `recurring_plan.reactivated_as_new_plan`. This event triggers when a supporter reactivates a canceled recurring plan and the organization's Donor Portal reactivation setting is configured to create a new plan. In that case Fundraise Up closes the original plan and starts a new one. The event is reported on the original plan that was reactivated — its `recurring_plan` is the ID of that original plan. ### August 2026 #### Added cancellation_reason and cancellation_details to recurring plan responses Added `cancellation_reason` and `cancellation_details` to responses for `GET /v1/recurring_plans` and `GET /v1/recurring_plans/{id}`. `cancellation_reason` indicates the reason category selected when the plan was canceled; `cancellation_details` contains any additional details provided by the supporter. Both fields can be `null` when the corresponding information was not provided or when the plan is not canceled. Possible values for `cancellation_reason`: `financial_difficulty`, `life_changes`, `switched_donation_method`, `change_in_giving_preferences`, `subscription_consolidation`, `loss_of_confidence_in_organization`, `technical_error`, `created_by_mistake`, `no_clear_reason_given`, `other`. ### June 2026 #### Added employment information to donations, recurring plans, and supporters Donation and recurring plan responses now include `employment_status` and `occupation` fields in the `supporter` object. Supporter responses include the same fields at the top level. These fields are collected for US political organizations as required by FEC regulations. For other organizations, these fields return `null`. `POST /v1/donations` and `POST /v1/donations/{id}` now accept `employment_status` and `occupation` in the `supporter` object. For political organizations, `employment_status` is required; when set to `employed`, `occupation` and `employer` are also required. #### Added campaign and designation management endpoints New endpoints for managing designations, designation groups, and campaigns via the API. The endpoints support programmatic creation, update, and deletion of designations, assignment to campaigns and designation groups, and campaign discovery. #### Added campaigns endpoints - `GET /v1/campaigns` — list campaigns with pagination and filtering by account or designation. - `GET /v1/campaigns/{id}` — retrieve a single campaign by ID. #### Added designations management endpoints - `GET /v1/designations` — list designations with pagination and filtering by campaign or creation date. - `GET /v1/designations/{id}` — retrieve a single designation. - `POST /v1/designations` — create a designation. - `POST /v1/designations/{id}` — update a designation. - `DELETE /v1/designations/{id}` — delete a designation. - `POST /v1/designations/batch/create` — create up to 100 designations in a single request. - `POST /v1/designations/batch/update` — update up to 100 designations in a single request. - `POST /v1/designations/batch/delete` — delete up to 100 designations in a single request. Batch operations process each item independently and return per-item results, allowing partial success. #### Added designation groups endpoints - `GET /v1/designation_groups` — list designation groups with full tree hierarchy (designations and nested groups). - `GET /v1/designation_groups/{id}` — retrieve a single designation group with its children. - `POST /v1/designation_groups/{id}/designations/assign` — assign designations to a group (up to 100 per request). - `POST /v1/designation_groups/{id}/designations/unassign` — remove designations from a group (up to 100 per request). #### Added campaign designation assignment endpoints - `POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/designations/assign` — assign designations to a campaign (up to 100 per request). - `POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/designations/unassign` — remove designations from a campaign (up to 100 per request). #### Updated `POST /v1/donations` `POST /v1/donations` now supports BACS Direct Debit. Pass a Stripe `bacs_debit` payment method in `payment_method.stripe.id` together with `payment_method.stripe.setup_intent_id`. BACS is available only for UK organizations and donations in GBP, supports recurring donations only (not one-time), and does not support the daily frequency. ### May 2026 #### Added endpoint for one-time Upgrade Links The new `POST /v1/upgrade_links/donations/{id}` endpoint returns a permanent Upgrade Link for a specific one-time donation. The link directs the supporter to a page where they can start a recurring plan based on their original donation. The donation must be eligible for upgrade. If it isn't (for example, tribute donation, inactive payment method, already upgraded), the endpoint returns a `422` error. To call this endpoint, your API key must have the **Upgrade Links — Write** permission. You can add this permission to a new API key or to an existing one in [**Dashboard > Settings > API keys**](https://dashboard.fundraiseup.com/settings/api-keys). #### Added `one_time_to_recurring_upgrade_link` field to donation responses The `GET /v1/donations` and `GET /v1/donations/{id}` endpoints now accept the `include=upgrade_link` query parameter. When you pass it, the response includes a `one_time_to_recurring_upgrade_link` field with the upgrade URL. The field is null for non-eligible donations. ### April 2026 #### GET /v1/events — `payments` field added; `donation` and `recurring_plan` deprecated `transaction_attempt.*` events now include a `payments` array. Each item in the array has `donation` and `recurring_plan` fields and represents one donation or recurring plan in the transaction. This replaces the top-level `donation` and `recurring_plan` fields, which are now deprecated. **What to do:** Switch from reading the top-level `donation` and `recurring_plan` fields to reading each object in `payments[]`. See the [migration guide](https://fundraiseup.com/support/migrating-deprecated-api-fields/). **Deadline:** The deprecated fields will be removed on **2026-10-30**. #### Added fee calculation endpoint - `GET /v1/donations/fee` — calculates the processing fee for a given donation amount and currency. Returns the fee amount and the total amount including the fee. #### Updated `POST /v1/donations` - Added optional `fee_amount` field. When provided, the fee amount is added to the donation total and recorded as supporter-covered fee. Use `GET /v1/donations/fee` to calculate the correct fee before submitting the donation. To use these endpoints, your API key must have the **Donations — Write** permission enabled. #### Added hide_amount to the tribute sharing in donation and recurring plan responses Added `hide_amount` to the `tribute.sharing` object in responses for `GET /v1/donations` and `GET /v1/recurring_plans`. The field indicates whether the donation amount should be hidden in the tribute notification sent to the recipient. #### Updated `POST /v1/donations` Added optional `payment_method.stripe.setup_intent_id` field. Required for ACH US Direct Debit payments. ### March 2026 #### Added grouped_donation_id to donation and recurring plan responses Added `grouped_donation_id` to responses for `GET /v1/donations`, `POST /v1/donations`, and `GET /v1/recurring_plans`. The field indicates the donation group identifier and can be used to correlate multiple donation items processed in the same payment. The field can be `null` when not applicable. #### Added source_of_funds to donation and recurring plan responses Added `source_of_funds` to responses for `GET /v1/donations`, `POST /v1/donations`, and `GET /v1/recurring_plans`. The field indicates the source of funds for the donation and is used to determine Gift Aid eligibility. Possible values: `own_money`, `on_behalf_of`, `fundraising_or_collection`. ### February 2026 #### Updates to the designation field The `designation` field now has stricter behavior across the API. When creating a donation, this field is required and must contain the ID of an existing designation in your account. Default values are no longer applied, and the API returns an error if the field is missing. In all responses of `/donations` and `/recurring_plans`, the designation field is now always populated and never null. #### Added designation configuration API endpoints: - `GET /v1/designation_configurations` - `GET /v1/designation_configurations/{id}` These endpoints allow you to read designation configurations. Each configuration represents a relationship between a designation and a campaign: - Configuration identifier and creation date - `repeat` field (enum: `one-time`, `recurring`, `all`) indicating which payment types are accepted for this designation-campaign combination - Account, campaign, and designation details The list endpoint supports filtering by `repeat`, `designation`, and `campaign`. To use these endpoints, your API key must have the **Designation configurations — Read** permission enabled. You can add this permission when creating a new API key or by updating an existing key in **Dashboard > Settings > API keys**. #### Added donation_benefit.updated event type to GET /api/v1/events The `types` field now includes a new allowed value: `donation_benefit.updated`. This event triggers when the recipient name or shipping details are updated on a benefit. Previously, these edits did not generate an API event, which caused data to fall out of sync between Fundraise Up and connected CRMs. ### January 2026 **Granular API key permissions** **Breaking Changes:** - Removed support for Donor Portal access links in Test mode. A request with `livemode: false` returns a `403 Forbidden` error. A request with `livemode: true` and a test supporter or recurring plan ID returns a `404 Not Found` error. - All new API keys require explicit `livemode` parameter in all GET and POST requests, regardless of whether they have permissions for one mode or both. - Legacy API keys (created before this release) cannot be edited through Dashboard. **New Features:** - Granular API key permissions: assign independent read/write permissions for each resource (donations, supporters, events, recurring plans, fundraisers). - Dual-mode API keys: a single key can have different permissions for Live and Test data simultaneously. ### December 2025 #### Added user agent field to device object for donation API endpoints: - `GET /api/v1/donations` - `GET /api/v1/recurring_plans` `user_agent` field contains the raw user agent string from the browser and can be `null` if not provided. #### Enhanced device information in recurring plans The `device` object has been enhanced for `GET /api/v1/recurring_plans` endpoint. Now it includes: - `ip` - Contains details about the IP address from which the donation was made. - `browser` — Browser name, can be `null` if not detected - `os` — Operating system name, can be `null` if not detected - `type` — Device type, can be `null` if not detected ### November 2025 #### Added benefit data to donation API endpoints: - `GET /api/v1/donations` - `GET /api/v1/recurring_plans` Both endpoints now return a `benefit` object with different states: - `state: "not_shown"` — benefits were not displayed during checkout - `state: "shown_not_selected"` — benefits were displayed but not selected - `state: "selected"` — a benefit was selected, includes full benefit details #### Added date filtering capabilities to API exports: - Introduced `created` parameter with `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, and `lte` operators for filtering donations, fundraisers, and other entities by creation date - Date values must be provided in RFC 3339 date-time format (ISO 8601 profile) with timezone - Added `created_at` field to fundraiser responses in `GET /v1/fundraisers` and `GET /v1/fundraisers/{id}` endpoints - Date filters can be used independently or in combination with existing parameters such as `ending_before`, `starting_after`, and `limit` ### July 2025 #### Bank account details now included in payment object The payment object in the `/v1/donations` response now includes a new `bank_account` object. This object is returned when the payment method is a bank transfer (such as ACH or SEPA Direct Debit) and includes a `last4` field with the last four digits of the bank account number. This addition mirrors the existing `credit_card` object and provides more complete data for reconciliation and reporting. No changes are required on your end unless you wish to make use of the new field. #### New field: supporter_covered_fee_in_default_currency A new field, `supporter_covered_fee_in_default_currency`, has been added to the `/v1/donations` response. It represents the equivalent of `supporter_covered_fee` in the organization’s default currency, providing better clarity for cross-currency donations. The description of `supporter_covered_fee` was also updated to clarify that the amount is in the donation’s currency. ### June 2025 #### New concurrency limit for API requests We’ve updated how rate limits work in the API. Instead of per-second or per-minute thresholds, the API now enforces a concurrency-based limit: each account can have up to 3 active requests at the same time. If this limit is exceeded, additional requests are rejected with a `429 Too Many Requests` error. #### Automatic updates for supporter contact data The address, phone, and employer fields in the `/v1/supporters` and `/v1/supporters/{id}` responses now reflect the latest data submitted through donations and recurring plans. To track changes, use the `supporter.updated`, `donation.updated`, and `recurring_plan.details_updated` events from the `/v1/events endpoint`. ### May 2025 #### Expanded data in recurring_plan object The `recurring_plan` object in the `/v1/donations` response now includes `created_at`, `ended_at`, and `next_installment_at` fields. This helps reduce the need for separate API calls to `/v1/recurring_plans/{id}`. ### April 2025 #### New endpoint: Fundraisers We’ve added a new `fundraisers` endpoint to the API. This endpoint lets you create, update, and retrieve supporter-created Fundraisers linked to your campaigns.

tags.name: Access links
tags.description: The Access link object represents link that grant supporter access to their Donor Portal.

tags.name: Campaigns
tags.description: The Campaign object represents a fundraising campaign. Every donation connects to a campaign. It includes settings such as enabled donation frequencies, designation mode, and status.

tags.name: Designation configurations
tags.description: The Designation configuration object represents a single designation configuration.

tags.name: Designation groups
tags.description: The Designation group object represents a container for related designations and other designation groups in your Fundraise Up account.

tags.name: Designations
tags.description: The Designation object represents a fund allocation for a donation, such as restricted or unrestricted giving.

tags.name: Donations
tags.description:
The Donation object represents a single donation. It can be either a one-time donation or an installment as part of a recurring plan.

You can create donations, update donations and associated recurring plans sourced from the API, and read donations from your account.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: The Event object represents each entry in your Audit Log, allowing you to track changes in your account.

tags.name: Fundraisers
tags.description: The Fundraiser object represents a supporter-created fundraising page linked to a campaign. You can create Fundraisers through the API, update them, and retrieve Fundraisers from your account.

tags.name: Recurring plans
tags.description: The Recurring Plan object represents a single recurring donation plan. It includes supporter data, which is displayed as it appears on the Recurring Plan page in your Dashboard.

code.description: Custom identifier for the organization, set as the Account code in the Fundraise Up account.

id.description: Unique identifier of the organization in the format A[A-Z]{7}.
